hook: Write the same news twice, once for a friend and once for the record.
intro: The question here is not whether you can write German but whether you can choose which German. Write the same piece of news twice: once to a colleague you like, once as a formal notice. The facts stay identical. Only the register moves, and it moves on two axes at once, the words and the sentence shapes. Write 1200 to 2500 characters for both together. The commonest failure is a leak: one gehobenes word in the chatty version, or one spoken particle in the formal one. The correction will hunt for exactly that.
tips[0].title: Register moves on two axes
tips[0].text: Words carry some of it, structure carries the rest. Formal German reaches for nouns, the passive and the impersonal; informal German reaches for verbs, active subjects and short main clauses. Moving only the words leaves a text that still sounds spoken.
tips[0].check.why: The passive and the nominalisation carry the formal register.
tips[0].trap: Over-formality in a message to a friend is a register mistake too, and it is the one most people make once they have learnt the formal words.
tips[1].title: Neutral is not formal
tips[1].text: Most German words are neutral: Geld, beginnen, sagen, bekommen. They fit both versions, and they are the backbone of each. Only a few words are genuinely marked: kriegen is informal, erhalten is formal, bekommen is neither. Hunt for the marked ones; leave the rest alone.
tips[1].check.why: kriegen is informal and erhalten formal; bekommen sits between them.
tips[2].title: Impersonal, not evasive
tips[2].text: The formal version may drop the personal subject, but it must not lose who is responsible. „Es wurden Fehler gemacht“ hides the agent; „Die Abteilung hat den Termin versäumt“ is just as formal and still says who. The difference is noticed.
tips[2].check.why: It stays formal and still names whose error it was.
remember[0]: Two axes: the words and the structures. Move both or neither.
remember[1]: Most words are neutral; only a few are marked. Hunt the marked ones.
remember[2]: Formal may be impersonal, but it must not hide who did what.
remember[3]: A single leaked word gives the whole version away.
exam: Writing the same content in two registers is a C2 task, and it is what anyone drafting at work does every day without noticing.
mistakes[0].why: The frame is formal and the sentence is not: a leak.
mistakes[1].why: Over-formality in an informal context is also a register error.
mistakes[2].why: Formal does not have to mean agentless.
mistakes[3].why: kriegen is informal; the Sie around it is not.
